n73cb71fa0d1.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
n73cb71fa0d1.x: Ajita Kesakambalin represented materialism. Gosala led the Ajivikas and Sanjaya Belatthiputta was the skeptic.

ne6f3fd94589.s: The decline of the Ajivikas and other heterodox sects is mainly attributed to:
o: The spread of Greek rule in the north-west
The Puranic-Bhakti revival and loss of royal patronage
The adoption of Ajivika doctrines by Buddhism
ne6f3fd94589.x: The heterodox traditions declined with the Puranic-Bhakti revival (including under the Pallavas) and the loss of royal patronage.

na9f951cc78a.s:
Consider the following about Ajivika patronage:
1. The Ajivikas were popular under Bindusara.
2. Ashoka donated the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas.
3. The Barabar caves were constructed by Chandragupta Maurya.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
na9f951cc78a.x: The Ajivikas were popular under Bindusara and Ashoka donated the Barabar caves to them; the caves were not constructed by Chandragupta Maurya.

nb4f7329c82f.s:
Consider the following about Lokayata:
1. It left no surviving texts of its own.
2. Its complete original canon survives in the Brihaspati Sutra.
3. It is known mainly through the criticisms of opposing schools.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nb4f7329c82f.x: Lokayata left no surviving texts and is known mainly through the criticisms and refutations of rival traditions, so statement 2 is wrong.

n45e598c875c.s: The Shramana movements of the sixth century BCE arose in the context of:
o: The Greek invasions of the north-west
The revival of Vedic ritualism in the Deccan
n45e598c875c.x: The Shramana reaction (Jainism, Buddhism, Ajivika and Charvaka currents) arose amid urbanisation and Magadhan patronage in the sixth century BCE.

nindian-history-17-15.s:
Consider the following:
1. Sudas fought a confederacy of ten kings in the Battle of Ten Kings.
2. The Battle of Ten Kings is described in the Rigveda.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-history-17-15.x: Sudas of the Bharatas fought a confederacy of ten kings, and the battle is described in Rigveda Mandala VII, near the Parushni (Ravi).

nindian-history-20-1.s: Darius I, who annexed parts of north-western India, ruled Persia during:
nindian-history-20-1.x: Darius I ruled Persia from 522 to 486 BC and annexed parts of north-western India.

n05aac64f75b.s: According to Herodotus, the Indian satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire paid a tribute of:
n05aac64f75b.x: Herodotus called the Indian satrapy the most populous and fertile; it paid 360 talents of gold dust, said to be one-third of the empire's revenue.

n0d6e2ffcc21.s: Which term for an inscription, used in Ashokan edicts, reflects the Darius (Persian) model?
n0d6e2ffcc21.x: The terms lipi/dipi, along with an opening in the third person shifting to the first person, show the Darius model in Ashokan edicts.

n95fb24a42a4.s:
Consider the following:
1. Persian contact left a lasting influence on Indian script and art.
2. Alexander's nineteen-month campaign left a lasting political mark on India.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n95fb24a42a4.x: Persian contact in the sixth–fifth centuries BC left lasting influences on script and art, while Alexander's nineteen-month campaign left almost no lasting political mark.

nindian-history-21-2.s: Which of the following about Alexander's Indian campaign is NOT correct?
o: Alexander fought Porus at the Hydaspes
Alexander's army was stopped at the Ravi
Alexander's army refused to go beyond the Beas
The Hydaspes is identified with the Jhelum
nindian-history-21-2.x: Alexander's army refused to go beyond the Beas, not the Ravi. He fought Porus at the Hydaspes, the Jhelum.

n19e731ccb67.s: Which feature of the Nanda kingdom is said to have deterred Alexander from marching farther east?
n19e731ccb67.x: The huge army of the Nanda kingdom deterred Alexander from advancing east, though Dhana Nanda was unpopular for heavy taxation.

nindian-history-39-16.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dhanananda – Indian ruler who supported Alexander
nindian-history-39-16.x: Agrammes was the Greek name of Dhanananda, the Magadha ruler; Bhaddasala was his commander and Ambhi supported Alexander.

nd194c2fb026.s: A major commercial consequence of Alexander's invasion was:
o: Closure of the north-western land routes
Opening of direct contact and new land and sea routes between Greece and India
Persian control over Indian trade routes
The end of contact between Greece and India
nd194c2fb026.x: The invasion opened direct contact between Greece and India and encouraged new land and sea routes.

nf5370932b53.s: By destroying several small north-western states, Alexander's invasion cleared the way for the rise of:
nf5370932b53.x: The invasion weakened the small north-western states, helping Chandragupta, who expelled the Greek satraps with Porus (Parvataka) as an ally.

nad7e267408b.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dated items)
nad7e267408b.s: Alexander's invasion of India is regarded as:
o: The first Persian conquest of India
The first dated event of Indian history
The beginning of the Saka era
The end of the Nanda dynasty
nad7e267408b.x: Alexander's invasion is regarded as the first dated event of Indian history, and Greek accounts help fix Mauryan chronology.

na93491a2e09.s:
Kautilya is also known by which of the following names?
1. Chanakya
2. Pushyagupta
3. Vishnugupta
Which of the above is/are correct?
na93491a2e09.x: Kautilya is also called Chanakya and Vishnugupta; Pushyagupta was a governor associated with the Sudarshana lake.

ne09554b880a.s: Which of the following pairs of source and subject is correctly matched?
o: Mahavamsa and Dipavamsa – Genealogies of Mauryan kings
ne09554b880a.x: Parishishtaparvan describes Chandragupta's Jain end; the Puranas give genealogies, the Divyavadana has Ashokan legends and the Mahavamsa/Dipavamsa cover Buddhism in Lanka.

nff8dfaf8c94.s:
Consider the following about Ashokan edicts:
1. James Prinsep first deciphered them in 1837.
2. The Greek-Aramaic edict of Ashoka was found at Girnar near Junagadh.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nff8dfaf8c94.x: Prinsep deciphered the edicts in 1837. The Greek-Aramaic edict is at Shar-i-Kuna (Kandahar); Girnar/Junagadh is linked with Rudradaman's inscription.

nc3308d0fb48.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the territories ceded by Seleucus I Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya?
nc3308d0fb48.x: The ceded territories were Aria, Arachosia, Paropanisadai and Gedrosia; Bactria was not among them.

n5310858fb05.s:
Consider the following about the Maurya–Seleucid alliance:
1. Seleucus's daughter Helena was married to Chandragupta Maurya.
2. Seleucus married Chandragupta's daughter.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n5310858fb05.x: The treaty tradition states that Seleucus's daughter Helena was married to Chandragupta Maurya, not the other way round.

n2022493dbad.s:
Consider the following about the last phase of Chandragupta Maurya's life:
1. He abdicated and became an ascetic.
2. He died by Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n2022493dbad.x: Jain tradition states that Chandragupta abdicated, became an ascetic and died by Sallekhana (fasting to death) at Shravanabelagola.

n4da70a507b9.s: The twelve-year famine in Chandragupta Maurya's time is traditionally linked with:
o: The split of Buddhism into Mahayana and Hinayana
The migration of the Ajivikas to the south
The division of Jains into Digambaras and Svetambaras
n4da70a507b9.x: The famine tradition is linked with the split between the Digambaras (Bhadrabahu) and the Svetambaras (Sthulabhadra).

nindian-history-1-10.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
nindian-history-1-10.x: Pushyagupta was Chandragupta Maurya's governor who built the Sudarshana lake; Tushasp was Ashoka's governor who added canals, and Rudradaman I repaired the lake.

nc255f3f2589.s: Who is regarded as the first Greek envoy to an Indian court?
nc255f3f2589.x: Megasthenes was the first Greek envoy to an Indian court, at Chandragupta Maurya's court.

n9ccf7662b46.s:
Consider the following about the Barabar caves:
1. They are located at Girnar.
2. They are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves.
3. They are carved in granite.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n9ccf7662b46.x: The Barabar caves in Bihar are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves, carved in granite; they are not at Girnar.

n8c32697e57c.s:
Consider the following about the origin of the Mauryas:
1. Brahmanical sources link the name Maurya with the Shudra woman Mura.
2. Buddhist and Jain sources describe Chandragupta as a Kshatriya of the Moriya clan.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n8c32697e57c.x: Brahmanical sources connect the name Maurya with Mura, while Buddhist and Jain traditions make Chandragupta a Kshatriya of the Moriya clan.

n151d51650d2.s: Which of the following pairs of Ashokan titles and meanings is correctly matched?
n151d51650d2.x: Devanampiya means 'beloved of the gods' and Piyadasi 'of pleasing looks'.

n3fd415455ff.s:
Consider the following about the Kalinga edicts:
1. The Separate Edicts at Dhauli and Jaugada address officials at Tosali and Samapa.
2. Major Rock Edict XIII appears at Dhauli and Jaugada in its usual form.
3. The Separate Edicts stress just treatment of the people.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n3fd415455ff.x: Major Rock Edict XIII is absent at Dhauli and Jaugada; these sites have Separate Edicts to officials at Tosali and Samapa stressing just treatment of the people.

nb68dffebf8f.s:
Arrange in chronological order by Ashoka's regnal year:
1. Rajukas receive independent judicial authority
2. Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya
3. Appointment of Dhamma Mahamatras
4. Quinquennial tours of rajukas, pradeshikas and yuktas
nb68dffebf8f.x: Dhammayatra (11th year), quinquennial tours (12th), Dhamma Mahamatras (14th), judicial authority to rajukas (26th).

nindian-history-5-23.s: Which name in Ashoka's Rock Edict XIII is correctly matched with the Hellenistic king it denotes?
nindian-history-5-23.x: Antikini is Antigonus Gonatas; Turamaya is Ptolemy II, Antiyoka is Antiochus II and Maka is Magas of Cyrene.

nindian-history-1-3.s: Who was the first scholar to read Ashoka's edicts?
nindian-history-1-3.x: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837 and was the first to read Ashoka's edicts.

nindian-history-1-49.s:
Consider the following about the Kanaganahalli inscription:
1. It is located in Karnataka.
2. It is associated with the Bhima river.
3. It contains the words 'Ranyo Ashoka'.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-history-1-49.x: Kanaganahalli lies in Karnataka on the Bhima river and carries a portrait panel labelled 'Ranyo Ashoka'.

n6b356693286.s:
Consider the following:
1. Brahmi was the source of the Telugu script.
2. Brahmi was used only for writing Telugu.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n6b356693286.x: Brahmi is the source of the Telugu script, but it was not restricted to Telugu; most Ashokan edicts across the empire used it.

nindian-history-1-2.s: Which Ashokan edict site is correctly matched with its script or language?
nindian-history-1-2.x: Kandahar (Shar-i-Kuna) is bilingual in Greek and Aramaic. Shahbazgarhi is in Kharosthi, Taxila in Aramaic and Girnar in Brahmi.

nindian-history-1-4.s: Which of the following about the Kharosthi script is NOT correct?
o: It was used in north-western India
Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra are Ashokan examples of it
It was the script of most Ashokan inscriptions
It was written from right to left
nindian-history-1-4.x: Most Ashokan inscriptions are in Brahmi; Kharosthi, written right to left, was used only in the north-west, as at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra.

n15bbf160418.s: Which Major Rock Edict is correctly matched with its subject?
o: Rock Edict III – Dhammayatras replace pleasure tours
Rock Edict VIII – Quinquennial tours of officials
Rock Edict III – Pativedakas may report at all times
Rock Edict VI – Pativedakas may report at all times
n15bbf160418.x: RE VI deals with Pativedakas and the king being available at all times; RE III covers quinquennial tours and RE VIII Dhammayatras.

n57b6ff3d6ae.s: The main evidence for determining the extent of Ashoka's empire is the:
n57b6ff3d6ae.x: The geographical spread of Ashokan edict sites is the principal evidence for the extent of his empire.

nindian-history-26-2-24.s:
Consider the following:
1. Dhauli is associated with Ashokan rock edicts and Kalinga.
2. Jaugada is associated with Ashokan rock edicts and Odisha.
3. Besnagar is associated with the Heliodorus Pillar and the Bhagavata religion.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-history-26-2-24.x: Dhauli and Jaugada in Odisha carry Ashoka's Kalinga rock edicts, and Besnagar (Vidisha) has the Heliodorus (Garuda) Pillar linked to the Bhagavata religion.

nindian-history-1-94.s:
Consider the following about Ashoka's visit to Lumbini:
1. He visited Lumbini when he had been consecrated twenty years.
2. The visit is recorded in the Rummindei pillar inscription.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-history-1-94.x: The Rummindei pillar records that Ashoka visited Lumbini after twenty years of his consecration; the eighth year refers to the Kalinga War.

nd60b2114a5e.s: Ashokan pillar edicts are concentrated in the Ganga plain mainly because:
o: River transport eased the movement of the heavy monoliths
Rock surfaces for edicts were absent there
Pillars were reserved for Buddhist monasteries
The pillars marked the route of the Kalinga campaign
nd60b2114a5e.x: The pillar edicts cluster in the Ganga plain because river transport made it easier to move the heavy monoliths.

nindian-history-1-1.s: Ashokan inscriptions are classified into which three groups?
nindian-history-1-1.x: Ashokan inscriptions are rock (major and minor rock edicts), pillar and cave (Barabar) inscriptions; copper-plates, seals and coin legends belong to later periods.

n6d8ccd5665e.s: The sculptures of Dharanikota are described as:
o: Later than those of Sanchi and Bharhut
Older than those of Sanchi and Bharhut
n6d8ccd5665e.x: Dharanikota sculptures, in the Amaravati region, are described as older than those of Sanchi and Bharhut.

nda3d0b5e30b.s: Which Mauryan revenue term is correctly matched with its meaning?
o: Sita – Pasture land and its dues
nda3d0b5e30b.x: Pranaya was the emergency tax or 'gift of affection'; Sita was income from crown land and Vivita pasture land and its dues.

nbca09bbc14d.s:
Consider the following about Bhaga in the Mauryan revenue system:
1. It was an emergency levy imposed during war.
2. It was normally the king's one-sixth share of the produce.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nbca09bbc14d.x: Bhaga was the king's share of agricultural produce, generally one-sixth (Megasthenes gives one-fourth to one-sixth); the emergency levy was Pranaya.

ndc9a81c1fb4.s:
According to Megasthenes:
1. The king was regarded as owner of all land.
2. Land revenue was collected directly by royal officials.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
ndc9a81c1fb4.x: Megasthenes stated that the king owned all land and that royal officials collected the revenue directly.

n027291ba8c9.s:
Consider the following about Mauryan agriculture:
1. Sita land was cultivated exclusively by free peasants.
2. The state gave seed, cattle and tools as relief during drought and famine.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n027291ba8c9.x: The state provided seed, cattle and tools as famine relief; Sita land also employed slaves and hired labourers.

n51b7998e6e9.s:
Consider the following about the Mauryan economy:
1. Good roads and state incentives encouraged crafts.
2. Merchants, artisans and shrenis financed early Buddhist centres, including those in Andhra.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n51b7998e6e9.x: Good roads and state incentives encouraged crafts, and merchants, artisans and shrenis financed early Buddhist centres, including in Andhra.

n2864e07ba99.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tamralipti – Principal port of the Ganga basin
n2864e07ba99.x: Tamralipti was an east-coast port, the principal port of the Ganga basin; Sopara and Bharukachchha were west-coast ports.

n8b42130d836.s:
Consider the following about Dakshinapatha:
1. It was the great southern trade route.
2. It was the northern highway from Taxila to Tamralipti.
3. The Krishna–Godavari delta was one of its nodes.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n8b42130d836.x: Dakshinapatha was the great southern route with the Andhra Krishna–Godavari delta as a node; the Taxila–Tamralipti highway was Uttarapatha.

nfcdb61eda0c.s:
Consider the following about Mauryan imperial currency:
1. It consisted mainly of punch-marked silver coins.
2. The coins bore portraits of the emperors.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nfcdb61eda0c.x: Mauryan currency was mainly punch-marked silver coins carrying symbols such as peacocks and hills, not portraits.

n699f923309e.s: Which was the most famous centre of learning during the Mauryan period?
n699f923309e.x: Taxila was the most famous Mauryan-period centre of learning, ahead of Ujjain and Varanasi.

ndc00cbe1e4e.s: Yaksha worship was shared by which religious traditions?
ndc00cbe1e4e.x: Yakshas were revered in Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism alike.

n721b01aaea7.s: Which of the following were among the exports of the Mauryan period?
n721b01aaea7.x: Diamonds, pearls, muslin and fine textiles were among the exports of the period.

n31d34b8f905.s: Which Mauryan pillar capital is correctly matched with its site?
n31d34b8f905.x: The bull capital is from Rampurva; the four-lion capital is from Sarnath, the single lion from Lauriya Nandangarh and the elephant from Sankisa.

nindian-history-66-1.s: Which stupa is correctly matched with its location?
o: Amaravati Stupa – Right bank of the Krishna, Andhra Pradesh
nindian-history-66-1.x: Amaravati is on the right bank of the Krishna; Sanchi is in Raisen, Bharhut in Satna and Dhamek at Sarnath.

nc737ca38ddf.s: Which of the following is cited as evidence of the financial crisis of the later Mauryas?
o: Increase in the purity of silver coins
Debasement of later punch-marked silver coins with more alloy
nc737ca38ddf.x: The higher alloy content of later punch-marked silver coins is read as evidence of fiscal strain and debasement.

n48516619c0d.s:
Consider the following about the Pushyamitra Sunga persecution debate:
1. The Divyavadana describes Pushyamitra as a persecutor of Buddhists.
2. Sanchi and Bharhut grew under Sunga rule, which complicates this claim.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n48516619c0d.x: The Divyavadana calls Pushyamitra a persecutor of Buddhists, but the growth of Sanchi and Bharhut under Sunga rule points the other way.

n7320cbd2864.s:
Consider the following about the end of the Kanva dynasty:
1. Its last ruler was Susharman.
2. Susharman was overthrown by Menander.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n7320cbd2864.x: The last Kanva ruler, Susharman, was ended by the Andhras (Satavahanas), not by Menander.

nab728fda15d.s: According to the Chulla-Kalinga Jataka, the king of Assaka (Asmaka) defeated the king of:
nab728fda15d.x: The Chulla-Kalinga Jataka records the Kalinga–Assaka conflict in which the king of Assaka defeated the king of Kalinga.

nc7c03ce785c.s: The Bavari legend suggests that Buddhist ideas reached the Godavari region:
nc7c03ce785c.x: The Bavari legend indicates that Buddhist ideas had reached the Godavari region before Mauryan expansion.

n2a7c70a3341.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
n2a7c70a3341.x: Mulaka had its capital at Pratishthana; Assaka (also called Asmaka) had its capital at Bodhan, and Andhra lay on the Dakshinapatha route.

n3a71a765611.s:
Consider the following about early Andhra:
1. Andhra lay outside the major trade routes.
2. Merchant guilds of Andhra used Kalingapatnam and later Masulipatnam.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n3a71a765611.x: Andhra formed part of the Dakshinapatha trade route, and its merchant guilds used Kalingapatnam and later Masulipatnam.

o: The Satavahana conquest of the Deccan
n6b8869608ee.x: Mudrarakshasa concerns Chandragupta Maurya and the establishment of Mauryan power, so it is not used for the Yavana invasion in Pushyamitra's reign.

nindian-history-29-4.s: Which founder is correctly matched with the ruler he replaced?
nindian-history-29-4.x: Vasudeva Kanva replaced Devabhuti; Pushyamitra replaced Brihadratha Maurya and Simuka replaced Susharma.

nindian-history-4-21.s: Which founder is correctly matched with his dynasty?
nindian-history-4-21.x: Nannuka founded the Chandelas; Gopala founded the Palas, Nanyadev the Karnata dynasty and Anangpal the Tomars.

nindian-history-28-2.s: Which of the following dynastic successions in Magadha is NOT correct?
nindian-history-28-2.x: The Mauryas came before the Kanvas; the order was Maurya, Shunga, Kanva, and the Nandas followed the Shishunagas.

nindian-history-27-4.s: Who founded the Kanva dynasty by overthrowing the last Shunga king?
nindian-history-27-4.x: Vasudeva Kanva overthrew the last Shunga king and began the Kanva dynasty.

nb8c7686292e.s: The Sunga court encouraged a revival of which language, in contrast to Ashoka's use of Prakrit?
nb8c7686292e.x: The Sunga court encouraged a revival of classical Sanskrit, whereas Ashoka had used Prakrit.

necc0ae39fb0.s:
Consider the following about Bharhut:
1. Its inscriptions record only royal donations by the Mauryan emperors.
2. Its inscriptions name guilds of ivory workers and stone carvers who financed it.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
necc0ae39fb0.x: Bharhut's inscriptions mention guilds of ivory workers and stone carvers who contributed to the monument.

nf3048057a4a.s:
The Sunga period is associated with:
1. Brahmanical revival
2. The rise of Bhagavatism
3. The development of stone Buddhist art
Which of the above is/are correct?
nf3048057a4a.x: The Sunga period saw Brahmanical revival, the rise of Bhagavatism and the development of stone Buddhist art.

nindian-history-143-6.s: Which of the following about Pushyamitra Shunga is NOT correct?
o: The Ayodhya inscription records his two Ashvamedhas
Patanjali is linked with his Ashvamedha ceremonies
He was a senapati before founding the dynasty
nindian-history-143-6.x: Pushyamitra performed two, not three, Ashvamedha yajnas, as the Ayodhya inscription records.

n42fe8c1ced0.s: Bactria, where Greeks settled after Alexander, lay in present-day:
n42fe8c1ced0.x: Bactria was in north Afghanistan, where Greek settlers established themselves after Alexander's campaigns.

n10861534a06.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
n10861534a06.x: The Taxila copper plate belongs to Patika; Gandhara art is Kushana, the Junagadh inscription Rudradaman I's and Milindapanho is about Menander.

n466e05803bb.s:
Consider the following:
1. Indo-Greek coins are noted for royal portraits and bilingual legends.
2. Kushana coinage is associated with large-scale gold issues and many deities.
3. Kushana coins preceded Indo-Greek coins in using royal portraits.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n466e05803bb.x: Indo-Greek coins are known for portraits and bilingual legends, and Kushana coinage for large-scale gold and many deities; Kushana coins did not precede Indo-Greek portraits.

na90d1dc6e3c.s: Indo-Greek coins are the main source for reconstructing:
o: The list of more than 30 Indo-Greek kings
na90d1dc6e3c.x: Indo-Greek coins are the principal source for the list of more than 30 Indo-Greek kings.

nf94c50e7cf3.s: Which branch of the Western Kshatrapas is correctly matched with its region?
nf94c50e7cf3.x: The Kshaharatas held the Western Deccan, while the Kardamakas ruled around Ujjain, Malwa and Kathiawar.

n56c95b1f78a.s:
Consider the following about Western Kshatrapa coinage:
1. Their principal coins were exclusively gold.
2. Their silver coins are numerous in western India.
3. Kardamaka silver coins carried Saka-era dates.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n56c95b1f78a.x: Numerous Western Kshatrapa silver coins are found in western India and Kardamaka silver coins bear Saka-era dates; their coinage was not exclusively gold.

n81b1bea9b32.s: Which Satavahana ruler defeated Nahapana of the Kshaharata dynasty and restruck his coins?
n81b1bea9b32.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated the Kshaharata ruler Nahapana and restruck his coins as an assertion of Satavahana power.

nindian-history-9-4.s: Which era is correctly matched with its starting year?
nindian-history-9-4.x: The Kalachuri/Chedi Era began in 248 AD; Vikrama Samvat in 57/58 BC, the Kali Era in 3102 BC and the Harsha Era in 606 AD.

nindian-history-9-2.s: Which of the following about the Saka Samvat is NOT correct?
o: Saka year plus 77 gives the AD year
nindian-history-9-2.x: The AD year is the Saka year plus 78, not 77; the era began in 78 AD with Kanishka and Chaitra is its first month.

n0ab87d7aafd.s: The era of 78 CE is usually credited to Kanishka, but some accounts credit which ruler with starting the Salivahana era?
n0ab87d7aafd.x: Some accounts credit Gautamiputra Satakarni with starting the Salivahana era, though the 78 CE era is commonly credited to Kanishka.

n8a2e6e3a7e1.s: The era beginning in 78 CE came to be called the Saka era because it was used by:
o: The Western Kshatrapas in their records and coins
n8a2e6e3a7e1.x: The Western Kshatrapas, who were Sakas, used the era on their records and coins, so it became known as the Saka era.

nindian-history-142-6.s:
Consider the following about Kanishka and China:
1. Chinese texts call Kanishka's people the Yue-chi.
2. The Kushanas defeated the Chinese force of Pan Chao in 86 AD.
3. The Kushanas marched against Pan Chao after a Han princess was refused to Kanishka.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-history-142-6.x: After a Han princess was refused to Kanishka, the Kushanas (the Yue-chi of Chinese texts) marched against Pan Chao in 86 AD and lost to a smaller Chinese force.

nindian-history-142-16.s:
Consider the following about the Saka Samvat:
1. It began 135 years before the Vikrama era.
2. Many historians consider Kanishka its originator, beginning in 78 AD.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-history-142-16.x: Many historians credit Kanishka with starting the Saka era in 78 AD; it began 135 years after, not before, the Vikrama era (57 BCE).

nindian-history-142-18.s: Which of the following about the Rabatak inscription is correctly matched?
nindian-history-142-18.x: The Rabatak inscription was found near Surkh Kotal in Afghanistan in 1993; it uses the Greek script and the Bactrian language.

nindian-history-142-29.s:
Which of the following cities are mentioned in the Rabatak inscription?
1. Saketa
2. Kaushambi
3. Sri Champa
Select the correct answer:
nindian-history-142-29.x: The Rabatak inscription says Kanishka's rule reached Saketa, Kaushambi, Pataliputra and Sri Champa.

nindian-history-142-25.s:
Which of the following works are attributed to Ashvaghosha?
1. Saundarananda
2. Buddhacharita
3. Sariputraprakarana
Select the correct answer:
nindian-history-142-25.x: Saundarananda, Buddhacharita and Sariputraprakarana are all works of Ashvaghosha.

n1eaf8b01f13.s: According to I-tsing, Nagarjuna's Suhrllekha was:
o: Recited only at the Satavahana court
n1eaf8b01f13.x: I-tsing recorded that he saw students in India memorising Nagarjuna's Suhrllekha.

n880d77e4041.s: Which military development is associated with the Shakas and Kushanas?
o: Improved cavalry and wider use of saddles and reins
n880d77e4041.x: The Shakas and Kushanas improved cavalry and promoted the wider use of saddles and reins.

n9283e9940da.s:
Consider the following about Gandhara art:
1. It predominantly expressed Mahayana Buddhism.
2. It represented the Buddha only through symbols.
3. It commonly depicted Bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteshvara and Maitreya.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n9283e9940da.x: Gandhara art mainly expressed Mahayana Buddhism and showed the Buddha with Bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteshvara and Maitreya, not only through symbols.

n8061ca324c2.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gandhara – Slender figures showing intense movement
Mathura – Muscular, robust and smiling figures
n8061ca324c2.x: Slender, dynamic and emotional figures are typical of Amaravati; Gandhara is known for realistic, Apollo-like faces and spiritual calm.

n7b71ed1bf5a.s:
Consider the following about the anthropomorphic Buddha image:
1. The Buddha was first widely shown in human form in the Kushana period.
2. Whether Gandhara or Mathura made the first such image is debated.
3. Only Amaravati produced the first anthropomorphic Buddha image.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n7b71ed1bf5a.x: Both Gandhara and Mathura produced Buddha images in human form in the Kushana period (1st century CE), and their priority is debated; Amaravati was not the first.

n8e96c1b6155.s: Before human images became established, the Buddha was represented through:
o: Symbols such as throne, footprints, wheel, tree and stupa
n8e96c1b6155.x: Before anthropomorphic images, the Buddha was worshipped aniconically through the throne, footprints, wheel, tree and stupa.

n28f63b5ee57.s: Who publicised Amaravati art through the work 'Tree and Serpent Worship'?
n28f63b5ee57.x: James Fergusson publicised Amaravati art in Tree and Serpent Worship and called it the 'Epitome of Indian architecture'.

nc5c7ee7d503.s: The influence of Amaravati art spread to:
o: Sri Lanka, South-East Asia and later Gupta art
nc5c7ee7d503.x: Amaravati art influenced Sri Lanka (especially Anuradhapura), South-East Asia and later Gupta art.

ne4018363255.s: The Purna-Kumbha motif of Amaravati art forms the emblem of the:
ne4018363255.x: The Purna-Kumbha motif of Amaravati art is the emblem of the Andhra Pradesh State Government.

nbeff837cc1e.s: Which mudra is correctly matched with its gesture?
nbeff837cc1e.x: Varada is the lowered open palm of boon-giving; Abhaya is the raised right palm and Dhyana the hands in the lap.

n32e1dd124d7.s: The Satavahana centre was shifted east to Dhanyakataka (Amaravati) under:
n32e1dd124d7.x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi shifted the centre to Dhanyakataka (Amaravati) after Rudradaman's attacks.

n1fd81e9c003.s: Which of the following ruler–title pairs is NOT correctly matched?
n1fd81e9c003.x: Kavivatsala was Hala's title; Gautamiputra Satakarni bore titles such as Ekabrahmana, Ekashura and Shakasanhari.

nap-history-4-4.s: Which site is correctly matched with its feature?
o: Bhairavakonda – Centre of the Rajagirika school
Guntupalli – Centre of the Rajagirika school
Ajanta – Eight caves and centre of Saivism
nap-history-4-4.x: Guntupalli was the Rajagirika Buddhist centre; Ajanta has the Swetagaja Jataka painting, Nasik the cave inscription and Bhairavakonda the eight Saiva caves.

n232e8a4609a.s:
Consider the following about Gautamiputra Satakarni:
1. He belonged to the Kshaharata branch of the Western Kshatrapas.
2. He defeated Nahapana and recovered Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan and Nasik.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n232e8a4609a.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana and recovered these territories; it was Nahapana who belonged to the Kshaharata branch.

n5d241132aea.s: Which region of the Nasik Prasasti is correctly matched with its modern area?
n5d241132aea.x: Akara was East Malwa; Avanti was West Malwa, Aparanta North Konkan and Vidarbha Berar.

o: The high status of royal women, with succession remaining patriarchal
Election of kings by the queen mothers
Foundation of the dynasty by a queen
ne6880e41d0f.x: Metronymics reflected the high status of royal women and respect for the mother, while succession stayed patriarchal.

n2758e3e7377.s:
Consider the following about Satavahana queens:
1. Devi Naganika acted as regent during her son's minority.
2. Naganika was the queen of Hala.
3. Naganika was the wife of Satakarni I.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n2758e3e7377.x: Naganika, wife of Satakarni I, acted as regent during her son's minority; Lilavati was Hala's queen.
